# Rust Translation Specification for mimalloc 3.3.2
Generated at: 2026-05-29T21:39:36+00:00
## Status
This specification was generated before any Rust translation files were created. It is intentionally conservative: every scanned source, build, test, configuration, callback, environment, macro, type, global, function, method, and test helper symbol is listed with a planned Rust destination and translation strategy. Generated documentation and binary-only artifacts are explicitly excluded from translation and recorded below.

## Clarification: complete allocator-replacement scope

This file is now the complete implementation specification/checklist for a full mechanical Rust allocator replacement. Stage 001 code is only a first translated slice; the checklist below is the authoritative remaining work breakdown. Each symbol has an implementation task of the form “Implement/define/port/map `<symbol>` located in `<file>` lines `<range>`,” so the translation can proceed without silently skipping private symbols, tests, build definitions, environment options, or platform-specific branches.

## Repository Overview
- Detected languages: C11, C++17 test/header adapter code, C/C++ headers, CMake, shell/batch scripts.
- Project purpose: mimalloc is a low-level memory allocator with public C API, optional malloc/new/delete overriding, platform-specific OS memory primitives, arena/page/heap internals, statistics, options, and tests.
- Source directories: `include/`, `include/mimalloc/`, `src/`, `src/prim/*`.
- Test directories: `test/` with C and C++ API/override/stress/wrong-free tests.
- Examples: no separate `examples/` directory; `test/main.c` and override tests act as usage examples.
- Scripts: `bin/bundle.sh`, `bin/bundle.bat`; vcpkg helper CMake under `contrib/vcpkg/`.
- Build files: top-level `CMakeLists.txt`, `test/CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/*.cmake`, `mimalloc.pc.in`, IDE project files under `ide/`.
- CI files: `azure-pipelines.yml`, `.github/workflows/*.yml` present in archive.
- Dependency manifests: CMake and pkg-config template; no Rust Cargo manifest existed before translation.
- Generated files: `docs/` Doxygen HTML/JS/CSS assets are generated and excluded from translation as source; `doc/` contains source documentation/assets.
- Vendored/prebuilt files: `bin/mimalloc-redirect*.dll`, `*.lib`, `minject*.exe` are prebuilt Windows artifacts; source is not present.
- Documentation: `readme.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `doc/release-notes.md`, `doc/mimalloc-doc.h`, generated Doxygen under `docs/`.
- Public entry points: C API in `include/mimalloc.h`, stats API in `include/mimalloc-stats.h`, override macros in `include/mimalloc-override.h`, C++ new/delete/allocator support in `include/mimalloc-new-delete.h` and C++ portions of `include/mimalloc.h`.
- Binaries/libraries: CMake builds shared `mimalloc`, static `mimalloc-static`, object `mimalloc-obj`, and test executables; Windows redirect DLLs are packaged.
- External APIs: C runtime, POSIX `mmap`/`munmap`/`madvise`/`sysconf`, Windows `VirtualAlloc`/`VirtualFree`/ETW/TLS APIs, macOS malloc zones/interpose APIs, WASI/Emscripten APIs, Valgrind/ASAN/TSAN hooks, libc string/stdio/errno, pthread/Win32 threads in tests.
- Runtime assumptions: allocator can initialize before `main`, may replace malloc/free/new/delete, uses thread-local storage, atomics, low-level OS virtual memory, and must avoid allocating while formatting diagnostics.
- Platform-specific code: `src/prim/windows`, `src/prim/unix`, `src/prim/osx`, `src/prim/wasi`, `src/prim/emscripten`, and CMake architecture branches for x86/x64/arm/riscv.
- Unsafe/low-level behavior: raw pointer arithmetic, pointer encoding, free-list manipulation, page metadata, mmap/VirtualAlloc, optional guard pages, malloc override/interposition, atomics and TLS. Rust translation must use `unsafe` in these modules with local invariants documented.
- Concurrency behavior: extensive atomics (`_Atomic`, platform intrinsics), locks, abandoned page reclamation across threads, thread-local heaps, thread init/done hooks, and stress tests with OS threads.
- IO behavior: diagnostic/statistics output to callbacks/stderr/stdout; environment parsing; no network behavior found.
- Serialization formats: no persistent serialization schema; external formats are C ABI, CMake package files, pkg-config template, generated docs, and textual stats/options output.
- Database usage: none found.
- Environment variables: options are read as `mimalloc_<option>` (case transformed internally) with legacy aliases; all derived variables are in the inventory.
- CLI flags: no library CLI; `test/test-stress.c` accepts stress-test positional/options via `argc/argv`; CMake options are configure-time flags.
- Configuration files: CMake files, pkg-config template, vcpkg port files, IDE project files, CI YAML.
- Uninspectable/ambiguous parts: binary-only Windows redirect/minject artifacts; generated docs excluded; target-specific branches not executed on every platform.

## Rust Project Setup Decision
A single Rust library crate is the safest initial structure because the original project is primarily a library with optional C ABI exports and tests. The crate uses `src/lib.rs` with modules that correspond to original source clusters. No binary target is created initially because the original runtime entry points are library APIs and test executables. Future stages may add examples or feature-gated cdylib/staticlib crate types after core allocator semantics are translated.
Initial Cargo setup created after this spec: `Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/types.rs`, `src/options.rs`, and `tests/options.rs`. Stage 001 deliberately translates only declaration-level constants/types/options descriptors so it does not depend on untranslated allocator internals.

## Complete Mechanical Implementation Checklist

This section is the strict follow-along checklist requested for a complete allocator replacement. It does **not** say the allocator is already translated; it enumerates every symbol discovered in the included repository inputs and turns each into an explicit implementation task. A complete mechanical Rust translation is not done until every task below has status `translated` or a documented `not-applicable/external-binary/generated-artifact` disposition, and all validation commands pass on the target matrix.

- Implementation tasks: **3573**
- Dependency edges referenced by these tasks: **24400**
- Machine-readable checklist: `RUST_FULL_SYMBOL_IMPLEMENTATION_CHECKLIST.csv`
- Machine-readable dependency edges: `RUST_DEPENDENCY_EDGES.csv`
- Rule: implement tasks in stage order. Within a stage, implement declaration/type/configuration tasks before functions, function prototypes before callers, and SCC/cycle clusters together using the cycle strategy in the dependency-graph section.
- Rule: no public allocator API such as `mi_malloc`, `mi_free`, `mi_realloc`, heap APIs, page APIs, arena APIs, override APIs, or initialization APIs is complete until its direct dependencies and tests listed here have been translated or explicitly stubbed.

### Completion gate for this checklist

The full allocator replacement is complete only when:

1. Every implementation task above has an updated status of `translated`, `verified`, or a narrowly documented non-Rust disposition such as `generated-doc-excluded` or `binary-artifact-source-missing`.
2. Every edge in `RUST_DEPENDENCY_EDGES.csv` has either both endpoint symbols translated or a documented, tested Rust-safe stub/abstraction.
3. All cycle/SCC strategies listed in the dependency graph have been applied with explicit Rust ownership, lifetime, atomic, TLS, or unsafe invariants.
4. Public C ABI exports and optional allocator override behavior have target-specific tests or documented target exclusions.
5. `cargo fmt`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --all-targets`, `cargo test --all`, and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` pass in an environment with a Rust toolchain.

### Initialization-Order, Global-State, Unsafe/FFI, and Translation Clusters
- Initialization-order dependencies: `src/init.c`, `src/options.c`, `src/threadlocal.c`, and `src/static.c` coordinate process/thread initialization, output buffering, option initialization, and static bundling. Rust must use explicit `OnceLock`, `AtomicBool`, `thread_local!`, and carefully ordered initialization APIs.
- Global-state dependencies: options table, output/error callbacks, statistics counters, arena/page-map global state, OS memory limits, random contexts, and thread-local heaps. Rust translation should prefer explicit state structs where public ABI permits and atomics/locks for process globals where ABI requires singleton behavior.
- Unsafe/FFI dependencies: public C ABI, raw allocation/free pointers, OS virtual memory, C callbacks, malloc/new/delete overrides, Valgrind/ASAN/ETW hooks, and binary Windows redirect artifacts. Unsafe blocks must be localized and justified per module.
- Dependency clusters suitable for staged translation: declarations/options -> bits -> atomics/sync -> stats/random -> primitives -> OS memory -> bitmap/page-map -> pages -> arenas -> heaps/thread-local -> allocation/free -> adapters/overrides -> init/static -> C++ docs/interoperability -> tests.

Total translation stages: **16**. Stages are ordered by dependency cluster so that high-level allocation APIs are not translated before constants, types, helpers, platform abstractions, page/arena/heap state, and error/output dependencies exist or have documented stubs.

## Required Handling of Unknowns
### UNKNOWN-0001
Location: Whole repository

Symbol: All allocator fast/slow paths

Issue: Exact behavior depends on many compile-time cfg combinations and target OS/architecture; only the host/static CMake defaults were inspectable mechanically in this pass.

Evidence: CMake contains MI_SECURE, MI_PADDING, MI_TRACK_* and platform branches; source contains Windows/macOS/WASI/Emscripten code.

Conservative Rust approach: Represent every cfg branch in the plan; translate host-safe declarations first; add cfg stubs only with explicit status.

Test coverage: Stage 001 tests cover declarations/options only; later stages need target matrix.

Resolution needed: inspect/port target-specific behavior during the relevant stage or obtain missing source/artifact policy.

### UNKNOWN-0002
Location: src/prim/windows/prim.c and bin/*

Symbol: Windows redirect/interpose behavior

Issue: Prebuilt redirect DLL/lib artifacts are binary-only in the archive; source for minject/redirect module is not present.

Evidence: bin contains .dll/.lib/.exe files and readme; CMake links/copies redirect binaries on Windows.

Conservative Rust approach: Do not reimplement binary redirect behavior silently; expose as unsupported or require source/binary packaging decision.

Test coverage: No Rust test port in Stage 001.

Resolution needed: inspect/port target-specific behavior during the relevant stage or obtain missing source/artifact policy.

### UNKNOWN-0003
Location: Generated docs under docs/

Symbol: Generated Doxygen files

Issue: Generated HTML/JS assets are not source of truth and were excluded from translation inventory except as documentation evidence.

Evidence: docs/ contains Doxygen output; doc/ contains source docs/assets.

Conservative Rust approach: Translate source headers/code, not generated docs; keep docs excluded.

Test coverage: N/A.

Resolution needed: inspect/port target-specific behavior during the relevant stage or obtain missing source/artifact policy.

### UNKNOWN-0004
Location: C++ templates in include/mimalloc.h

Symbol: mi_stl_allocator and heap STL allocators

Issue: Rust does not have a direct C++ template ABI equivalent; behavior is relevant only for C++ consumers.

Evidence: Templates implement std::allocator interface and call mi_new/mi_free/heap APIs.

Conservative Rust approach: Document as C++ facade/interop concern; not part of core Rust allocator semantics unless a cxx bridge is added.

Test coverage: No direct Rust unit test in Stage 001.

Resolution needed: inspect/port target-specific behavior during the relevant stage or obtain missing source/artifact policy.
